title_en: Rules of Procedure of the National People's Congress of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en:
Article 2 The session of the National People's Congress shall be held in the first quarter of each year. The date of convening the session shall be decided by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and announced.
In case of special circumstances, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may decide to appropriately advance or postpone the session. Where the date for advancing or postponing the session cannot be decided at the current session, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may separately decide or authorize the Council of Chairmen to decide, and shall announce it.

Article 3 The session of the National People's Congress shall be convened by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. The first session of each National People's Congress shall be convened by the Standing Committee of the previous National People's Congress within two months after the election of the deputies to the current National People's Congress is completed.
Article 4 A session of the National People's Congress may be held only when more than two-thirds of the deputies are present.

Article 6 The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall, one month before the session of the National People's Congress is held, notify the deputies of the date of the session and the main items proposed for discussion, and shall distribute to the deputies the draft laws to be submitted to the session for deliberation.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may, before the session of the National People's Congress is held, organize deputies to study and discuss the relevant draft laws, solicit opinions of the deputies, and inform them of the relevant information concerning the main items to be discussed at the session.
The provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall not apply to an ad hoc session of the National People's Congress.

Article 7 Before the session of the National People's Congress is held, the deputies shall form delegations according to the electoral units. The plenary session of a delegation shall elect a leader and deputy leaders. The leader shall convene and preside over the plenary session of the delegation. The deputy leaders shall assist the leader in his work.
A delegation may be divided into several deputy groups. The group meeting of deputies shall elect group conveners.

Article 8 Before the session of the National People's Congress is held, a preparatory meeting shall be convened to elect the Presidium and the Secretary-General, and to adopt the agenda and decisions on other preparatory matters for the session.
The preparatory meeting shall be presided over by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. The preparatory meeting for the first session of each National People's Congress shall be presided over by the Standing Committee of the previous National People's Congress.
Each delegation shall deliberate on the draft list of the Presidium and the Secretary-General, the draft agenda, and other preparatory matters for the session proposed by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, and shall offer opinions.
The Council of Chairmen of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may, based on the opinions offered by the delegations, propose adjustments to the draft list of the Presidium and the Secretary-General, the draft agenda, and other preparatory matters for the session, and shall submit them to the preparatory meeting for deliberation.

Article 9 The Presidium shall preside over the session of the National People's Congress.
Decisions of the Presidium shall be adopted by a majority vote of all its members.

Article 11 The standing chairmen of the Presidium shall convene and preside over meetings of the Presidium. The first meeting of the Presidium shall be convened and presided over by the Chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. After the meeting elects the standing chairmen of the Presidium, the standing chairmen of the Presidium shall preside.

Article 12 Proposals and relevant reports shall be deliberated at plenary sessions of the delegations and at group meetings of deputies.
Proposals, questions, and motions for recall submitted in the name of a delegation shall be adopted by a majority vote of all the deputies of that delegation.

Article 13 The standing chairmen of the Presidium may convene meetings of leaders of delegations to hear the deliberative opinions of each delegation on major issues concerning proposals and relevant reports, to conduct discussions, and shall report the circumstances and opinions of the discussions to the Presidium.
The standing chairmen of the Presidium may, on major specialized issues, convene relevant deputies elected by the delegations for discussion; responsible persons of the relevant departments of the State Council shall attend the meetings, report on the situation, and answer questions. The circumstances and opinions of the discussion at the meetings shall be reported to the Presidium.
Article 14 The Presidium may convene a plenary session of the congress for speeches from the floor to express opinions on proposals and relevant reports.

Article 15 Deputies to the National People's Congress shall attend the session; if unable to attend due to illness or other special reasons, they shall request leave in writing from the secretariat of the session. The secretariat shall report to the Presidium the attendance of deputies and the reasons for absence.
Deputies shall diligently perform their duties, carefully deliberate on all proposals and reports, and strictly observe the discipline of the session.

Article 16 The members of the State Council, the members of the Central Military Commission, the Director of the National Commission of Supervision, the President of the Supreme People's Court, and the Procurator-General of the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall attend the session of the National People's Congress without voting rights; the responsible persons of other relevant organs and organizations may, upon decision by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, attend the session of the National People's Congress without voting rights.

Article 17 The session of the National People's Congress shall be held in public.
The agenda, schedule, and proceedings of the session of the National People's Congress shall be made public.
During the session of the National People's Congress, speeches made by deputies at various meetings shall be compiled into bulletins and distributed to the session, and, at the request of the deputy, the record or summary of the speech may be distributed to the session. The bulletins, speech records, or summaries may be in paper form or electronic form.
Public galleries shall be set up for the plenary sessions of the congress. The methods for public attendance shall be separately prescribed.

Article 18 Press conferences and press briefings shall be held during the session of the National People's Congress.
The session of the National People's Congress shall have a spokesperson, and delegations may, as needed, have spokespersons.
The secretariat may organize deputies and responsible persons of relevant departments and units to accept interviews by the news media. A delegation may organize the deputies of that delegation to accept interviews by the news media.
The plenary sessions of the congress shall be publicly reported through media such as radio, television, and the internet.

Article 19 The National People's Congress may, when necessary, hold a closed session. A closed session shall be held upon decision by a meeting of the Presidium attended by the leaders of all delegations, after the Presidium has solicited the opinions of the delegations.
Article 20 When the National People's Congress is in session, the secretariat and the relevant delegations shall arrange necessary interpretation for deputies from ethnic minorities.

Article 21 When holding a session, the National People's Congress shall arrange the schedule reasonably to improve the quality and efficiency of deliberation.
Each delegation shall conduct deliberations in accordance with the schedule of the session.

Article 22 The session of the National People's Congress shall utilize modern information technology to promote the digitalization of meeting documents and materials, and adopt methods such as online video to provide convenience and services for deputies in performing their duties.

Article 23 The Presidium, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the special committees of the National People's Congress, the State Council, the Central Military Commission, the National Commission of Supervision, the Supreme People's Court, and the Supreme People's Procuratorate may submit to the National People's Congress proposals that fall within the scope of its functions and powers, and the Presidium shall decide to place them on the agenda of the session.
A delegation or a group of thirty or more deputies jointly may submit to the National People's Congress proposals that fall within the scope of its functions and powers. The Presidium shall decide whether to place them on the agenda, or shall first refer them to the relevant special committee for deliberation and for an opinion on whether to place them on the agenda, and shall then decide whether to place them on the agenda, and shall distribute to the session the report on the handling opinions of the proposals adopted by the Presidium. When a special committee is deliberating, it may invite the proposer(s) to attend the meeting without voting rights and to express opinions.
A proposal jointly submitted by deputies or by a delegation may be submitted before the session of the National People's Congress is held.

Article 24 For proposals placed on the agenda of the session, the proposer(s) and the relevant special committee of the National People's Congress and the relevant working departments of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall provide relevant materials.

Article 25 For proposals placed on the agenda of the session, the proposer(s) shall submit an explanation on the proposal to the session. The proposal shall be deliberated by each delegation, and the Presidium may also refer it to the relevant special committee for deliberation and submission of a report, and the Presidium shall deliberate and decide to submit it to the plenary session of the congress for a vote.

Article 26 For a bill placed on the agenda of the session, after the plenary session of the congress hears the explanation on the bill, it shall be deliberated by each delegation and shall also be deliberated by the Constitution and Law Committee and the relevant special committee.
The Constitution and Law Committee, based on the deliberative opinions of the delegations and the relevant special committee, shall conduct a unified deliberation on the bill, and shall submit to the Presidium a report on the results of deliberation, a revised draft of the law or of the relevant legal issue, and shall explain important differing opinions in the report on the results of deliberation. After the Presidium has deliberated and adopted the report, it shall be distributed to the session. The revised draft shall be deliberated by each delegation, and the Constitution and Law Committee shall make further revisions based on the deliberative opinions of each delegation, and shall submit a final draft for a vote, which the Presidium shall submit to the plenary session of the congress for a vote.
The deliberative opinions of the relevant special committee shall be distributed to the session in a timely manner.
The procedures for deliberation and voting on a bill drafted and submitted by a specific law drafting committee established upon decision of the National People's Congress shall be separately prescribed.

Article 27 A bill to be submitted to the National People's Congress may, during the period when the National People's Congress is not in session, be first submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. After deliberation by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress in accordance with the relevant procedures, it shall decide to submit the bill to the National People's Congress for deliberation.
For a bill that the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress is to submit to the National People's Congress for deliberation, it shall publish the draft law to the public and extensively solicit opinions, except where the Council of Chairmen decides not to publish it. The time for soliciting opinions from the public shall generally be no less than thirty days.

Article 28 When a special committee deliberates proposals and relevant reports involving specialized issues, it may invite relevant deputies and experts to attend the meeting without voting rights and to express opinions.
A special committee may decide to hold a closed meeting.

Article 29 Where, for a proposal placed on the agenda of the session, the proposer(s) requests its withdrawal before it is submitted for a vote, the deliberation on the proposal by the session shall terminate upon the consent of the Presidium.

Article 30 Where, during the deliberation of a proposal placed on the agenda of the session, major issues arise that require further study, the Presidium may propose, and the plenary session of the congress may decide, to authorize the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress to deliberate and decide, and to report to the next session of the National People's Congress for the record or to submit to the next session of the National People's Congress for deliberation.

Article 31 Where a proposal submitted by a delegation or jointly by thirty or more deputies is decided by the Presidium not to be placed on the agenda of the current session, it shall be referred to the relevant special committee for deliberation after the National People's Congress is not in session. After the relevant special committee deliberates, it shall submit a report on the results of deliberation to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, and after the report is deliberated and adopted by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, it shall be distributed to the next session of the National People's Congress.

Article 32 The suggestions, criticisms, and opinions concerning the work of various aspects submitted by deputies to the National People's Congress to the National People's Congress shall be referred by the working office of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress to the relevant organs and organizations for study and handling, and shall be replied to within three months from the date of referral, and at the latest within six months. Where a deputy is not satisfied with the reply, he may submit opinions, and the working office of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall refer them to the relevant organs or organizations or their superior organs or organizations for further study and handling, and shall be responsible for replying.

Article 33 When the National People's Congress holds its annual session, the work reports submitted to the session by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the State Council, the Supreme People's Court, and the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall, after deliberation by each delegation, be subject to the session's adoption of corresponding resolutions.

Article 34 Forty-five days before the session of the National People's Congress is held, the relevant competent department of the State Council shall report to the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee of the National People's Congress and the relevant special committees on the main contents of the implementation of the national economic and social development plan for the previous year and the preliminary plan for the draft national economic and social development plan for the current year, and on the main contents of the implementation of the central and local budgets for the previous year and the preliminary plan for the draft central and local budgets for the current year. The Financial and Economic Affairs Committee shall conduct a preliminary examination. When conducting the preliminary examination, the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee shall invite deputies to the National People's Congress to participate.

Article 35 When the National People's Congress holds its annual session, the State Council shall submit to the session the report on the implementation of the national economic and social development plan for the previous year and the draft plan for the current year, and the draft national economic and social development plan; and the report on the implementation of the central and local budgets for the previous year and the draft budgets for the current year, and the draft central and local budgets. Each delegation shall examine them, and the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee and the relevant special committees shall also examine them.
The Financial and Economic Affairs Committee, based on the examination opinions of the delegations and the relevant special committees, shall examine the matters specified in the preceding paragraph, and shall submit a report on the results of examination to the Presidium. After the Presidium has deliberated and adopted the report, it shall be distributed to the session, and the Presidium shall submit to the plenary session of the congress for a vote the draft resolution on the implementation of the national economic and social development plan for the previous year and the national economic and social development plan for the current year, and the draft resolution on the implementation of the central and local budgets for the previous year and the central and local budgets for the current year.
The examination opinions of the relevant special committees shall be distributed to the session in a timely manner.

Article 36 Where the national economic and social development plan or the central budget, after being approved by the National People's Congress, must be partially adjusted during implementation, the State Council shall submit the adjustment plan to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for examination and approval.

Article 37 The examination, approval, and adjustment of the Five-Year Plan Outline for National Economic and Social Development and the medium- and long-term plan outline shall be carried out by reference to the relevant provisions of this Chapter.

Article 38 Candidates for the Chairman, Vice-Chairmen, Secretary-General, and members of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, candidates for the President and Vice-President of the People's Republic of China, candidates for the Chairman of the Central Military Commission, candidates for the Director of the National Commission of Supervision, candidates for the President of the Supreme People's Court, and candidates for the Procurator-General of the Supreme People's Procuratorate shall be nominated by the Presidium. After deliberation and consultation by the delegations, the Presidium shall, based on the opinions of the majority of the deputies, determine the list of official candidates.
Candidates for the Premier of the State Council and other members of the State Council, and candidates for members of the Central Military Commission other than the Chairman shall be nominated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Constitution.
Candidates for the chairpersons, vice chairpersons, and members of the special committees shall be nominated by the Presidium from among the deputies.
Article 39 The nominator of a candidate shall introduce the basic information of the candidate to the session and shall give necessary explanations on questions raised by the deputies.

Article 40 Elections or decisions on appointments at the session of the National People's Congress shall be conducted by secret ballot. A candidate shall be elected or a decision shall be adopted only when the number of votes obtained exceeds one-half of all the deputies.
When the plenary session of the congress holds an election or votes on an appointment proposal, a secret voting booth shall be set up.
The results of the election or vote shall be announced on the spot by the person presiding over the session. The number of votes obtained by each candidate shall be published.
Article 41 The specific methods for elections and decisions on appointments at the session of the National People's Congress shall be adopted by the plenary session of the congress.

Article 42 After the members of state organs elected or appointed by the National People's Congress are produced in accordance with statutory procedures, they shall publicly take a constitutional oath. The oath-taking ceremony shall be organized by the Presidium.

Article 43 If, during the session of the National People's Congress, members of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the President and Vice-President of the People's Republic of China, members of the State Council, members of the Central Military Commission, the Director of the National Commission of Supervision, the President of the Supreme People's Court, the Procurator-General of the Supreme People's Procuratorate, or members of the special committees of the National People's Congress submit resignations, the Presidium shall refer their resignation requests to each delegation for deliberation and shall then submit them to the plenary session of the congress for decision. If resignations are submitted when the congress is not in session, the Council of Chairmen shall refer the resignation requests to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for deliberation and decision.
Where the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress accepts the resignation of the Chairman, Vice-Chairmen, or Secretary-General of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the President or Vice-President of the People's Republic of China, the Premier, Vice-Premiers, or State Councilors of the State Council, the Chairman of the Central Military Commission, the Director of the National Commission of Supervision, the President of the Supreme People's Court, or the Procurator-General of the Supreme People's Procuratorate, it shall report to the next session of the National People's Congress for confirmation.
Where the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress accepts the resignation of a member of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, it shall report to the next session of the National People's Congress.
When the National People's Congress is not in session and the positions of the Premier of the State Council, the Chairman of the Central Military Commission, the Director of the National Commission of Supervision, the President of the Supreme People's Court, or the Procurator-General of the Supreme People's Procuratorate become vacant, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may respectively decide on an acting person from among the Vice-Premiers of the State Council, the Vice-Chairmen of the Central Military Commission, the Deputy Directors of the National Commission of Supervision, the Vice-Presidents of the Supreme People's Court, or the Deputy Procurators-General of the Supreme People's Procuratorate.

Article 44 The Presidium, more than three delegations, or more than one-tenth of the deputies may submit motions for the recall of members of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the President and Vice-President of the People's Republic of China, members of the State Council, members of the Central Military Commission, the Director of the National Commission of Supervision, the President of the Supreme People's Court, and the Procurator-General of the Supreme People's Procuratorate. The Presidium shall refer the motions to each delegation for deliberation and shall then submit them to the plenary session of the congress for a vote. Alternatively, in accordance with the provisions of Chapter VI of these Rules, the Presidium may propose, and the plenary session of the congress may decide, to organize an investigation committee, and the next session of the National People's Congress shall deliberate and decide on the basis of the investigation committee's report.
The motion for recall shall state the reasons for recall and provide relevant materials.
Before the motion for recall is submitted to the plenary session of the congress for a vote, the person proposed for recall shall have the right to present a defense at a meeting of the Presidium or at the plenary session of the congress, or to submit a written defense, which the Presidium shall distribute to the session.

Article 45 Where a deputy to the National People's Congress who is a member of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress or a member of a special committee is recalled by the original electoral unit, his or her position as a member of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress or as a member of a special committee shall be revoked accordingly, and the Presidium or the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall announce it.

Article 46 Where a member of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress or a member of a special committee requests to resign as a deputy to the National People's Congress and the request is accepted, his or her position as a member of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress or as a member of a special committee shall terminate accordingly, and the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall announce it.

Article 47 When each delegation deliberates proposals and relevant reports, the relevant departments shall send responsible persons to attend the meetings, listen to opinions, and answer questions raised by the deputies.
When the plenary sessions of the delegations deliberate the government work report, examine the report on the implementation of the national economic and social development plan for the previous year and the draft plan for the current year, and the draft plan, examine the report on the implementation of the central and local budgets for the previous year and the draft budgets for the current year, and the draft budgets, and deliberate the work reports of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the responsible persons of the State Council and its various departments, and the responsible persons of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate, or persons delegated by them, shall respectively attend the meetings, listen to opinions, and answer questions.
When the Presidium and the special committees deliberate proposals and relevant reports, the responsible persons of the State Council or the relevant organs shall attend the meetings, listen to opinions, answer questions, and may provide supplementary explanations on the proposals or relevant reports.

Article 48 During the session of the National People's Congress, a delegation or a group of thirty or more deputies jointly may submit in writing a question to the State Council and its various departments, the National Commission of Supervision, the Supreme People's Court, or the Supreme People's Procuratorate.
Article 49 A question must clearly state the subject of the question, the issues to be questioned, and the content.

Article 50 A question shall, in accordance with the decision of the Presidium, be answered orally by the responsible person of the organ questioned at a meeting of the Presidium, a meeting of the relevant special committee, or a meeting of the relevant delegation, or shall be answered in writing by the organ questioned. If the answer is given at a meeting of the Presidium or a special committee, the leader of the delegation or the deputy who submitted the question shall have the right to attend the meeting without voting rights and to express opinions.
If the deputy or delegation that submitted the question is not satisfied with the answer to the question, they may make a request, and upon decision by the Presidium, the organ questioned shall give another answer.
If the answer is given at a meeting of a special committee or a delegation, the relevant special committee or delegation shall report the circumstances of the answer to the Presidium.
When the Presidium deems it necessary, it may distribute the report on the circumstances of the answer to the question to the session.
If the question is answered in writing, the responsible person of the organ questioned shall sign it, and the Presidium shall decide to distribute it to the session.
Article 51 The National People's Congress may, when it deems it necessary, organize an investigation committee on a specific issue.

Article 52 The Presidium, three or more delegations, or one-tenth or more of the deputies jointly may propose to organize an investigation committee on a specific issue, which shall be submitted by the Presidium to the plenary session for decision.
The investigation committee shall be composed of one chairman, a number of vice-chairmen, and a number of members, nominated by the Presidium from among the deputies and submitted to the plenary session for approval. The investigation committee may engage experts to participate in the investigation.

Article 53 When the investigation committee conducts an investigation, all relevant State organs, social organizations, and citizens shall have the obligation to truthfully provide necessary materials to it. If a citizen providing materials requests the investigation committee to keep the source of the materials confidential, the investigation committee shall keep it confidential.
The investigation committee may, during the investigation, refrain from disclosing the investigation status and materials.

Article 54 The investigation committee shall submit an investigation report to the National People's Congress. The National People's Congress may, based on the investigation committee's report, adopt corresponding resolutions.
The National People's Congress may authorize the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress to hear the investigation report of the investigation committee when the National People's Congress is not in session, and may adopt corresponding resolutions, which shall be reported to the next session of the National People's Congress for the record.
Article 55 Deputies to the National People's Congress shall not be subject to legal investigation for their speeches and votes at various meetings of the National People's Congress.
Article 56 When speaking at various meetings of the National People's Congress, deputies shall focus on the topics determined by the meeting.

Article 57 A deputy who speaks at a plenary session may speak twice, with the first speech not exceeding ten minutes and the second speech not exceeding five minutes.
Those who request to speak at a plenary session shall register with the secretariat before the meeting, and the executive chairman of the session shall arrange the order of speeches; those who request to speak temporarily at a plenary session may speak only with the permission of the executive chairman of the session.

Article 58 A member of the Presidium, the head of a delegation, or a representative elected by a delegation who speaks at each meeting of the Presidium may speak twice on the same issue, with the first speech not exceeding fifteen minutes and the second speech not exceeding ten minutes. With the permission of the person presiding over the meeting, the speaking time may be appropriately extended.

Article 59 Voting on bills at plenary sessions shall be passed by a majority vote of all deputies.
Amendments to the Constitution shall be passed by a vote of more than two-thirds of all deputies.
The result of the vote shall be announced on the spot by the person presiding over the meeting.
When voting at the meeting, a deputy may vote in favor, vote against, or abstain from voting.

Article 60 Voting on bills at meetings shall be conducted by secret ballot using voting devices. If the voting device system malfunctions during use, voting shall be conducted by a show of hands.
Amendments to the Constitution shall be voted on by secret ballot.
The provisions of the first paragraph of this Article shall apply to the voting methods of preparatory meetings and meetings of the Presidium.

Article 61 The following persons elected by the National People's Congress: the Chairman, Vice-Chairmen, Secretary-General, and members of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress; the President and Vice-President of the People's Republic of China; the Chairman of the Central Military Commission; the Director of the National Commission of Supervision; the President of the Supreme People's Court; the Procurator-General of the Supreme People's Procuratorate; and the following persons decided to be appointed: the Vice-Chairmen and members of the Central Military Commission; and the approved members of the special committees of the National People's Congress shall be announced by the proclamation of the National People's Congress.
The Premier, Vice-Premiers, State Councilors, Ministers in charge of ministries, Chairpersons of commissions, the Governor of the People's Bank of China, the Auditor-General, and the Secretary-General of the State Council, who are decided to be appointed by the National People's Congress, shall be appointed by the President of the People's Republic of China by signing a presidential order in accordance with the decision of the National People's Congress and shall be announced.

Article 62 Where a member of a State organ resigns or is removed from office during a session of the National People's Congress, the announcement procedure provided in Article 61 of these Rules shall apply.
Article 63 Constitutional amendments adopted by the National People's Congress shall be announced by the proclamation of the National People's Congress.
Article 64 Laws adopted by the National People's Congress shall be promulgated by the President of the People's Republic of China by signing a presidential order.

Article 65 Laws, resolutions, decisions, proclamations issued by the National People's Congress, as well as explanations of draft laws, reports on deliberation results, etc., shall be promptly published in the Bulletin of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and on the website of the National People's Congress.
Article 66 These Rules shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
